was: Modern campground of Hartwick Pines State Park (9,335 acres, with the old-growth pines) near Grayling. Sites 1-64 have 20/30-amp electric with shared water spigots; sites 65-100 are full hookup with 50-amp. Trails from the campground to Bright and Glory lakes and a spur to the park's mountain-bike trails. --Claude

was: Modern campground in two loops by the Muskegon Lake navigation channel walkway: the first loop (sites 1-92) is adjacent to the channel, the second (sites 101-147) has larger sites near the big dune and Muskegon Lake. The channel walkway and its parking lot are closed for a U.S. Army Corps of Engineers project through Nov. 14, 2026 (DNR park page, read 2026-10-25). --Claude

was: Rustic campground in two loops (Oak #1-48, Poplar #49-99) atop 20-ft embankments overlooking Hardy Dam Pond, a 6-mile flooding of the Muskegon River; large private sites with 20- to 30-ft forested buffers. Boat launch between the loops with a few mooring spots for registered campers, buoyed swim area in the Poplar loop, kayak rentals at the office early June to mid-September, 18-hole disc golf; borders the Manistee National Forest. Spongy moth larvae can surge in summer. --Claude

was: Rustic state forest campground among red pines and hardwoods along the Upper Manistee River, 7.7 mi SW of Frederic via County Road 612 and Goose Creek Road; a narrow footpath runs along the water's edge, with a staircase to the river mid-campground and a path by site #16. Separate walk-in tent sites (parked a quarter mile SE) and a paddle-in/walk-in group area. Brown, brook and rainbow trout. The reservable Manistee backcountry/canoe sites are a separate USFS program. --Claude

was: Rustic state forest campground on shallow, warm-water Muskrat Lake, 12 mi NW of Mio via M-33 North, West Miller Road, Richardson Road and Muskrat Lake Road. Two sites accommodate a 40-ft vehicle/trailer (per an earlier DNR listing). Carry-in access to the lake; ORVs may ride between the campground and the trails (Mio ATV trail). Managed by Rifle River Recreation Area. --Claude

was: Quiet, shaded campground on the banks of the Pine River near the Silver Creek Pathway, 5.5 mi N of Luther via State Road; often fills up in summer. Sites 20-26 are walk-in tent sites on a small river peninsula. Undeveloped boat launch off the parking lot for paddlers and anglers (brown and rainbow trout). The Lincoln Hills cycle/ATV trails and ORV routes adjoin the campground. --Claude

was: Rustic state forest campground on the west side of Mio Pond, the Au Sable River impoundment at Mio Dam; secluded wooded sites. A separate paddle-in group camp sits on the east side. Managed by Rifle River Recreation Area. 2 mi NW of Mio via Morenci Avenue, Pond Drive and South Gerber Road. --Claude

was: Rustic campground in the Pretty Lake Quiet Area (non-motorized use only on Pretty Lake and its seven-lake chain), ~25 mi NW of Newberry via M-123 and County Roads 407 and 416. Only the 18 main-loop sites are drive-in; the walk-in/paddle-in sites lie along the Pretty Lake Pathway, with some short portages. Day-use picnic area; carry-in access ~50 yards from the parking area. --Claude

was: Private campground on the banks of the Maple River opposite public state land; large riverfront transient sites plus rustic and primitive sites, a boat launch and live bait for fishing. Most numbered sites away from the river are seasonal (operator's site map). --Claude

was: Small (8-acre) Christian family campground, owner-run since 1996 (the owners' daughter is taking over after 2025); 48 RV sites (partial & full hookup, 13 seasonal) plus 16 rustic tent sites and cabins. Alcohol and drug free: possession by anyone in the party is cause for eviction without refund. About 1 mile from Stony Lake and 2 miles from Lake Michigan public access; no on-site swimming/lake frontage. --Claude

was: Private wooded campground on M-115 in Tustin, SE of Cadillac; RV and rustic tent sites plus rental cabins, clubhouse, pool, mini-golf. Open May-Oct; nightly stays, and a discounted monthly rate by phone. --Claude

was: City of Harbor Beach municipal park (city-owned since 1903) on 40 acres at the north end of town, across N. Huron Ave (M-25) from Lake Huron; full-hookup modern sites, rustic sites in the woods, tent and group camping, nature trail, ball fields. Sites reported tightly spaced. --Claude

was: Village of Bellaire campground on Craven Pond, a mile east of downtown; full-hookup, water/electric and rustic sites, a walking loop nearby. Google Maps gives wrong directions: the entrance is at the end of E Broad St where it meets S Derenzy (Fairground) Rd. Camp host at site 30. --Claude

was: City of Gladstone campground at 37 Michigan Ave on Little Bay de Noc (Lake Michigan), with a 1,500-ft sandy beach and deck, a boardwalk and bike path, and a playground. Full-hookup, water-and-electric, electric-only and tent sites, with a mix of transient and seasonal campers. --Claude

was: City of Otsego municipal campground at the back of Brookside Park off M-89 along the Kalamazoo River. RV sites have concrete pads; water comes from 2 spigots shared across 3 sites (bring a splitter); a couple of tent sites too. Register and pay in person at the Otsego Police Department (127 Court St). --Claude

was: Oakland County Parks campground on Stewart Lake, 14555 Dixie Hwy, Holly; concrete or gravel pads, plus camping cabins, yurts and 12 group areas. Swimming beach, mini golf, skate park, paved trails. Daily/annual Oakland County vehicle permit required. --Claude

was: Huron County Parks (county government) campground, 6400 Main St, Caseville, on Saginaw Bay (Lake Huron), with one of the state's nicer beaches; the town's shops are walkable. Electric & water, full-hookup and lakefront full-hookup nightly sites plus seasonal and mobile-home sites; pavilions and a playscape. Tents not allowed on full-hookup sites. --Claude

was: City of Lake City park on 52 semi-wooded acres at 5547 W. Davis Road, four blocks east of Miltner Beach on Lake Missaukee (inland, not lakefront); playground, ball field, open green space and an 18-hole disc golf course with concrete tee pads. Many sites go to monthly and seasonal campers, so call ahead for a summer weekend. --Claude

was: Cedarville Township park on M-35 along the Bay of Green Bay: 10 acres with a picnic area and beach, about 29 miles north of Menominee. Not part of the Menominee County Parks system, though booked through its reservation site. One camper plus one tent (or two tents) per site. --Claude

was: Iron County park on Chicagon Lake (1630 County Rd 424, Crystal Falls). Beach (no lifeguard) with a changing house, waterfront cook stoves, playground; historic Chippewa (Ojibwa) burial grounds preserved on site. Opens the Friday before Memorial Day through September. --Claude

was: City of Ironwood campground beside the Gogebic County Fairgrounds on US 2, with shaded sites and a small playground.  9 sites have full hookups and the rest electric only. --Claude
